title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed sheet headed 'SYSTÈMES de RACINES (3) — Tribu n° 59'. 'La Tribu' was Bourbaki's internal bulletin, and this sheet appears to be part 3 of a Bourbaki summary on root systems. It sits among Grothendieck's handwritten notes on the motivic Galois group. The neighbouring pages are manuscript notes on fibre functors and points of motives (complex, real, ℓ-adic, Witt), so the typed sheet is probably either reused paper or reference material Grothendieck kept.

The page lists standard sources of root systems.

(II, end) For a real semisimple Lie algebra g with Cartan decomposition g = k + p and a maximal abelian subspace a ⊂ p, the spaces g^α = {x : [a,x] = α(a)x} define the restricted root system R ⊂ a* \ 0. It is in general non-reduced (it can be of type BC_n). Its Weyl group is the group of automorphisms of a induced by elements of Ad_g(k) that stabilise a.

(III) For a connected semisimple algebraic group G over a field k with a maximal k-split torus T and character group X*, cocharacters form the dual X_* of X*. The nonzero weights of T on Lie(G) form the relative root system of Borel–Tits. It is reduced when T is a Cartan subgroup, i.e. T equals its centraliser, i.e. G is k-split; this always holds when k is algebraically closed. The relative Weyl group is N_G(T)/Z_G(T). For k = C this recovers the root system of a Cartan subalgebra (case I). For k = R, the real points of Lie(T) are conjugate to a, recovering the restricted roots of case II.

(IV) For a compact connected semisimple Lie group G with maximal torus T, let X = Hom_cont(T, C*). The nonzero weights of T on g form a reduced root system in X ⊗ Q, with Weyl group N(T)/T. One has Q(R) ⊂ X ⊂ P(R), with X = P(R) when G is simply connected and X = Q(R) when G is adjoint.

All of this is the standard dictionary found in Bourbaki Lie VI §4 and its later chapters, Borel–Tits (1965), and Helgason. Within the archive it only serves as background: Tannakian/motivic Galois groups are reductive groups, which is where root data enter.
errors: In II the eigenspace condition is typed '[a,x] = (a).x'; it should read α(a).x. This is a typing slip in the original.
'T un tore algébrique sur G' should read 'dans G' (a maximal k-split subtorus of G). This is a slip in the original.
'Réduit si T est aussi un sous-groupe de Cartan' means T equals its centraliser, i.e. G is split. The statement is correct but phrased loosely.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed Bourbaki document (a 'Tribu' bulletin summary on root systems) filed among Grothendieck's motivic Galois notes. It contains only standard textbook material and no Grothendieck-specific mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The original indeed reads '(a).x' in II; the mathematically intended expression is α(a).x.
'Ad_g k' should be read as Ad_{g}(k), the adjoint group of the compact part k of the Cartan decomposition.
The heading 'Tribu n° 59' identifies the sheet as a Bourbaki internal document, not Grothendieck's own text.
